title: VPC change regret analysis - approval & audit PRD sketch
content:
Context / why this exists:
This is a working sketch to capture a short post‑mortem/regret analysis of recent customer VPC change flows that generated high-volume approval replays and long forensic retention costs. The goal: surface pragmatic PRD-level requirements we can add to the approval gate and audit pipeline so customers manage risk without paying for unnecessary retention or overwhelming oncall.

High-level problem statement:
- Customers doing customer-managed VPC config changes trigger our approval gates and generate full telemetry bundles. Some changes are repeated quick rollbacks or small firewall edits that still produce large evidence blobs (pcaps, syslog harvests, full operator screenshots).
- This results in two negative outcomes: 1) disproportionate storage/ingress costs in Private deployments and 2) noisy signals that make triage slow (SRE/customer ops must wade through large artifacts).
- We need a principled approach to classify, sample, and retain evidence: preserve forensics for high‑risk changes; minimize retention for low‑impact edits; preserve legal/contractual obligations.

Primary goals (measurable):
- Reduce average per-change audit payload size by 40% for low‑risk changes within 90 days of rollout (metric: bytes stored per approval event).
- Ensure triage time for approval escalations improves by 30% (metric: median time to root-cause with initial evidence bundle).
- Maintain >=99% retention coverage for "forensic-class" changes as defined by the approval policy (metric: fraction of high‑risk changes with full evidence retained).

Assumptions / constraints:
- Customers must be able to opt into stricter evidence retention for compliance-heavy accounts (legal/SLA override).
- Approval gates must remain fast (no synchronous blocking to assemble large evidence bundles).
- We cannot change customer VPC semantics; we can change what we collect, how we compress/filter, and how we index/search.
- Private deployments might have limited on‑prem object storage capacity.

User personas:
- Customer operator: wants minimal friction for frequent low-risk tweaks; needs a reliable rollback path.
- Enterprise security reviewer: needs complete evidence for audits and investigations.
- Redwood SRE/Support: needs quick, high-signal artifacts to diagnose failures and verify policies.

Core components proposed (sketch):
1) Approval risk classifier (lightweight):
   - Input signals: API call type, change delta size (lines/config keys), time-of-day, operator identity trust level, customer policy annotations, recent change frequency.
   - Output: risk bucket = {low, medium, high} + suggested retention policy id.
   - Implementation: simple rule engine + small ML classifier (later); start with deterministic heuristics.

2) Evidence minimizer pipeline (async):
   - Synchronous step: accept approval, store minimal metadata (diff, actor, timestamp, short text summary).
   - Async worker: gather full evidence only when risk bucket != low OR when policy requires. For low risk, run minimization and compress: strip PCAP payloads beyond headers, truncate logs to X lines, reduce screenshot resolution.
   - Benefits: keeps approval latency low; large artifact assembly run in background and can be GC'd faster.

3) Sampling + retention policy engine:
   - Per-customer defaults + per-approval override. Retention tiers: ephemeral (7d), standard (90d), forensic (indefinite / 7+ years as needed).
   - Sampling: store full evidence for first N changes in a window (e.g., first 3 changes to a given resource per 30d), then switch to minimized for repeated churn.

4) Compact search index & quick UI view:
   - Index the minimal metadata synchronously so SRE/ops can search by resource/actor/timestamp immediately.
   - Provide a "peek" view with trimmed artifact (first 200 lines, thumbnail) and a "retrieve full evidence" button that triggers on‑demand rehydration (subject to retention and access control).

Functional requirements (high level):
- FR1: Every VPC approval event must be assigned a risk bucket at the time of create (string).
- FR2: Minimal metadata must be stored synchronously within approval event (diff + actor + short description).
- FR3: Async evidence workers must be able to assemble full artifact bundles and mark them as "complete" or "minimized".
- FR4: Customers can set account-level retention defaults and per-resource overrides via Console API.
- FR5: Support on‑demand rehydration requests (audit retrieval) with access logging.

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR1: Approval latency (time to accept/reject) must not increase by more than 50ms median from current baseline for low-risk changes.
- NFR2: Evidence minimizer must achieve at least 5x compression for PCAP-heavy artifacts in typical cases.
- NFR3: Privacy: minimized artifacts must redact keys/creds following existing redaction rules.

Telemetry & audit details (proposal):
- Synchronous payload schema (small): {approval_id, actor_id, resource_id, risk_bucket, diff_hash, timestamp, policy_id}. Stored in primary DB.
- Evidence manifest (async): {approval_id, artifact_types:[syslog, pcap, screenshots], sizes, storage_uri, retention_tier, created_at}. Logged to audit log and emitted to customer SIEM integrations if enabled.
- Metrics to emit: approval_latency_ms, evidence_bundle_size_bytes, compression_ratio, rehydration_count, search_hit_latency.

Approval gate UX flow (sketch):
- Operator submits change -> gate evaluates risk -> gate responds (approved/needs-review) quickly based on policy.
- If needs-review or high risk: present full evidence capture checklist to operator (auto-populate recommended justification fields).
- For low risk: present a compact confirmation with an optional checkbox to request full evidence retention.

Edge cases / escalation:
- If evidence rehydration is requested but previously GC'd: create a ticketing flow (customer-facing) that describes what can be reconstructed and expected timeline.
- If classifier mislabels a high-risk change as low: allow retroactive evidence upgrade for a short window (e.g., 48h) and trigger audit of classifier decisions.
- Legal hold: immediate override to retain all artifacts regardless of bucket. UI must show active holds per-account.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): prototype deterministic rule engine + minimal metadata capture; instrument metrics.
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): implement async evidence worker and minimizer; enable for 10% of private deployments (opt-in beta).
- Phase 2 (8 weeks): add sampling policies, per-customer console controls, and rehydration API.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): evaluate ML classifier, SLO tuning, and expand to 100%.

Success metrics (initial):
- Storage delta: percent reduction in evidence storage for opted-in customers after 60 days.
- Operator satisfaction: CS survey score on approval flow friction.
- Incident triage time: median time to first actionable artifact.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Define deterministic heuristics for risk buckets (TBD: change size thresholds).
- Q2: Legal/regulatory mapping — what counts as "forensic-class" for GDPR, SOC2, and EU data residency? (need legal input).
- Q3: GC policy for minimized artifacts and recovery guarantees — acceptable RTO for rehydration?
- Q4: Can we reuse existing telemetry compression libraries (investigate Lucene-friendly index for diffs)?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight: the objective is to stop the "collect everything forever" default that is causing ongoing costs and operator overhead.
- We should prioritize deterministic heuristics and policy controls so customers can opt into stricter behavior for compliance.
- Marco/Evelyn: can you sketch a minimal API payload that the approval gate emits synchronously? I think we can re-use the current approval webhook with two small fields (risk_bucket, diff_hash).
- Ryan: can you run a quick sampling of last 30 days of approval artifacts and return distribution of artifact sizes (helpful to choose compression targets).

Quick checklist before next review:
- [ ] Draft risk bucket rules (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Legal mapping meeting (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Telemetry instrumentation PR (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Sample compression run and numbers (owner: Ryan)

End of sketch.

-- Aisha
(notes: this doc will be turned into a formal PRD after runway validation and an SRE cost analysis)
